topics.title: Performance debugging tools for Constellation applications

elements.description: A slow interaction can arise in the client, application server, rule processing, database or external service. Reproduce the reported path and use guardrail warnings plus measured evidence. A high compliance score is useful but does not prove the absence of performance defects.

elements.text: Worked example: A lookup is slow only for a large account. Capture its query volume and duration before treating it as a general frontend problem.

elements.description: Rule assembly generates and compiles executable code for rules; rule caches avoid repeating resolution and retrieval. Newly deployed rules can make initial use slower. Compare cold and warm behavior; numerous distinct ruleset lists can increase cache resource demands.

elements.text: Worked example: After a release, the first use of a rule is slower than repeats. Compare assembly and cache metrics to avoid measuring only the initial compile as steady-state behavior.

elements.description: Use PAL deltas to locate database cost, then inspect expensive statements with Database Trace and database tools. Consider filters, indexes, reporting-property optimization, data volume and transaction boundaries. Do not add arbitrary indexes or expose sensitive columns without analyzing the query and data requirements.

elements.text: Worked example: A report filters on an unoptimized property inside case data. Confirm the query plan and reporting requirements before optimizing the relevant property and retesting.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Performance debugging tools for Constellation applications

elements.description: Constellation uses stateless DX API requests with significant client orchestration. Inspect browser network/timing information and trace the relevant Service REST processing. Request context differs from a traditional stateful portal session; use the trace's step-page context rather than assuming a persistent portal Clipboard.

elements.text: Worked example: For a slow Constellation action, inspect its API request and response, trace the relevant Service REST rule and compare client rendering time with server processing time.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Single tier assumption
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every slow screen is caused by the database.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Locate the tier from actual timings.

examPitfalls.title: Cold versus warm
examPitfalls.trapDescription: One first-run timing represents steady-state performance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Users report one specific search is slow. What is the best initial diagnostic step?

options.text: Assume all UI code must be replaced
Double every pool without measurements
Delete all guardrail warnings
Reproduce that search and collect timings for the involved tiers

practiceQuiz.rationale: A reproducible path and timing evidence locate the cause. Unmeasured blanket changes can miss the actual bottleneck.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An application has a strong guardrail compliance score. Which conclusion remains unsupported?

options.text: Measured performance should still be tested
Warnings can guide improvement
Every production interaction meets its response-time target
Guardrail checks were considered

practiceQuiz.rationale: Guardrails reduce design risk, but runtime performance depends on workload and environment as well as rule configuration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A newly deployed rule is slow on first use but faster on later runs. Which process may explain part of this difference?

options.text: A work queue deletes the rule
Rule assembly and caching
Field auditing always stops after one run
Case authorization disappears

practiceQuiz.rationale: First-use generation/compilation and cache warm-up can add cost that differs from subsequent execution.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should numerous different ruleset lists be considered in a cache investigation?

options.text: Distinct lists can increase rule-cache resource demand
Ruleset lists never affect runtime
Every list is a new database table
They guarantee that no assembly occurs

practiceQuiz.rationale: Rule cache behavior depends on ruleset-list contexts. Excessive diversity can consume additional resources.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A report's PAL delta is dominated by database time. What should the next investigation examine?

options.text: Only the browser theme
Only the case name
Only the exam duration
The costly SQL operations, predicates and relevant query plan

practiceQuiz.rationale: Database evidence narrows the next step to the actual statements and access patterns.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A filter on a case-data property triggers a reporting-performance warning. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Ignore data sensitivity and expose all columns
Remove the report without investigating
Review property optimization and query design, then measure the change
Optimize every property indiscriminately

practiceQuiz.rationale: Optimize according to measured query needs, accounting for storage and security effects rather than blanket changes.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Constellation user action is slow. Which TWO evidence sources are useful?

options.text: Only a Field Value label
Browser network and rendering timings
Trace of the relevant DX Service REST processing
Only a traditional portal's assumed persistent Clipboard

practiceQuiz.rationale: Constellation diagnosis needs client timing and the stateless request's server execution context.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is a traditional persistent portal Clipboard assumption unsuitable for every Constellation API request?

options.text: Constellation requests are stateless and must be inspected in their own processing context
Constellation never runs server rules
All case data lives only in the browser
DX APIs are always SOAP services

practiceQuiz.rationale: Stateless request processing still uses server rules, but the context must be inspected for the specific API call.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
